items.stimulus: A music conservatory keeps its collection of $4{,}800$ handwritten opera scores in a climate-controlled vault. The vault has a floor area of $60$ square meters.
items.stem: What is the density of manuscripts in the vault, in manuscripts per square meter?
items.explanation: Density is the amount divided by the space: $\frac{4{,}800 \text{ manuscripts}}{60 \text{ m}^2} = 80$ manuscripts per square meter. The units read manuscripts per square meter, which is what the question asks for.

A.why: You divided the area by the number of manuscripts ($\frac{60}{4{,}800}$). That gives square meters per manuscript, the flipped quotient, not manuscripts per square meter.

B.why: You made a place-value slip when dividing. $4{,}800 \div 60$ is $80$, not $8$. Check it: $8 \times 60 = 480$, not $4{,}800$.

D.why: You multiplied the manuscripts by the area. That gives manuscript-square-meters, which is not a density. Density is a quotient, amount ÷ space.

items.stimulus: A paleobotanist studying a silicified tree trunk finds that the petrified wood has a density of $4$ grams per cubic centimeter. A fragment of this wood has a mass of $96$ grams.
items.stem: What is the volume, in cubic centimeters, of the fragment?
items.explanation: Because density = mass ÷ volume, volume = mass ÷ density: $\frac{96 \text{ g}}{4 \text{ g/cm}^3} = 24 \text{ cm}^3$. The grams cancel, which leaves cubic centimeters.
